Event 1 · Balance-sheet runoff

Fed balance-sheet runoff announced

2017-09-20 · Window 2016-09 to 2018-09. Selection: 2017-09-05 BOS report · Official event source.

The Federal Reserve announced that balance-sheet normalisation would begin in October 2017, while leaving its policy-rate range at 1.00–1.25%. This event marker is the September announcement, not the first day of runoff.

What to compare: how the selected shares moved as the policy backdrop changed. Funding costs, earnings and other news can also influence prices; this window does not isolate the effect of runoff.

Reading this window: use the shared metric toggle for price changes, P/E or P/B. The vertical line marks the event’s publication month, not an exact-day trade. Gaps are not filled; price changes exclude dividends.

Event 2 · China tariffs

Initial U.S. Section 301 China tariffs take effect

2018-07-06 · Window 2017-07 to 2019-07. Selection: 2018-07-02 BOS report · Official event source.

The first tranche of additional U.S. Section 301 tariffs on Chinese products took effect on 6 July 2018. It applied a 25% additional duty to 818 tariff lines covering approximately US$34 billion of imports. USTR had announced this tranche in June.

What to compare: price paths across USA and Asian listings during a changing trade-policy backdrop. A listing market is not a measure of a company’s sales exposure to China, and other developments occurred during the window.

Reading this window: use the shared metric toggle for price changes, P/E or P/B. The vertical line marks the event’s publication month, not an exact-day trade. Gaps are not filled; price changes exclude dividends.

Event 3 · Pandemic response

Fed pandemic rate cut and purchases

2020-03-15 · Window 2019-03 to 2021-03. Selection: 2020-03-02 BOS report · Official event source.

On 15 March 2020, the Federal Reserve lowered its policy-rate range to 0–0.25% as the coronavirus outbreak disrupted activity and financial conditions. It also announced purchases of at least US$500 billion of Treasuries and US$200 billion of agency mortgage-backed securities.

What to compare: the depth and subsequent path of price changes across the fixed share sample. The pandemic, business restrictions and other policy actions overlap; monthly observations cannot identify the immediate announcement-day response.

Reading this window: use the shared metric toggle for price changes, P/E or P/B. The vertical line marks the event’s publication month, not an exact-day trade. Gaps are not filled; price changes exclude dividends.

Event 4 · Rate hikes

Fed raises target range

2022-03-16 · Window 2021-03 to 2023-03. Selection: 2022-03-01 BOS report · Official event source.

The Federal Reserve raised its policy-rate range to 0.25–0.50% on 16 March 2022 and indicated that further increases would likely be appropriate. Its statement cited elevated inflation and noted that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine added uncertainty and price pressure.

What to compare: differences in share-price paths through a tightening period. The chart covers the surrounding year, not just this decision; changes in earnings, energy prices and later policy decisions can also matter.

Reading this window: use the shared metric toggle for price changes, P/E or P/B. The vertical line marks the event’s publication month, not an exact-day trade. Gaps are not filled; price changes exclude dividends.

Event 5 · Rate cut

Fed cuts target range by 0.50 pp

2024-09-18 · Window 2023-09 to 2025-09. Selection: 2024-09-03 BOS report · Official event source.

On 18 September 2024, the Federal Reserve cut its policy-rate range by 0.50 percentage points to 4.75–5.00%. It cited progress on inflation and a more balanced assessment of employment and inflation risks, while continuing to reduce its securities holdings.

What to compare: which selected shares had higher or lower price changes across the following monthly snapshots. A rate cut does not ensure a positive share return; the observed paths also include company news and later economic developments.

Reading this window: use the shared metric toggle for price changes, P/E or P/B. The vertical line marks the event’s publication month, not an exact-day trade. Gaps are not filled; price changes exclude dividends.

Price changes exclude dividends. Retrieved Yahoo split factors are applied to BOS quoted prices; other corporate actions are not fully reconciled. Action-source failures or currency mismatches stay visible but are excluded from price-performance rankings and price-change medians. Large monthly moves are flagged for review and retained in rankings. These are provisional price comparisons, not investment total returns.

Bank of Singapore equity coverage report series. Each event links its selection report; table and chart tooltips retain individual observation dates. The original local Excel and CSV companions remain available.

Method, selection rules and limits

Grouped view: USA means United States listings. Asia combines China, Hong Kong and Taiwan listings; Singapore and Japan remain separate. All other listing markets form Rest of world. ADRs stay in their listing market. Groups pool the original country-selected cohorts; the top-decile selection is not recalculated at regional level. Taiwan is absent in snapshots without selected Taiwan listings, not imputed.

Price-change group heat maps use the median across all available, ranking-eligible selected listings in the group, not an average of country medians. Valuation heat maps instead use all available positive source multiples. Chart filters do not change these medians. Each panel’s highest/lowest rankings are recalculated within its chosen groups; missing endpoints and unresolved action checks are excluded. Top-ten views use up to ten eligible listings, with market cap then ticker breaking ties. Large-company views use the selection snapshot’s market cap, not today’s size. The default table order is market cap; month-header sorting changes that table only. Hidden review columns do not remove checks: company tooltips and this method retain the limitations.

P/E and P/B: these are the positive multiples printed under BOS’s Consensus Forward Estimates heading. The exact forecast horizon is not specified. They are not trailing ratios or percentage changes. Source multiples are not split-adjusted, interpolated or replaced with current values. Forecast revisions, rolling horizons and negative earnings/book values can limit comparisons. Missing, nonmeaningful and nonpositive multiples appear as gaps; available raw numeric values are retained in cell tooltips. Valuation group medians use available positive source ratios independently of the price-return eligibility checks. Highest/lowest filters and ribbons always refer to +12-month price performance, not valuation merit. The blue scale is descriptive and caps at 60× for P/E and 10× for P/B; values remain uncapped.

Fixed top decile of BOS-covered listings by positive USD billion market cap in latest pre-event report. Ceil(10% of eligible coverage), including cutoff ties. Country is listing market, not issuer domicile. Series key is exact ticker plus currency. No ticker-history splicing. Monthly slots are publication months, not month-end prices. Missing values are not filled. Change=(split-adjusted observation / split-adjusted pre-event baseline - 1)*100. Yahoo split actions are supplemental; dividends are excluded. Unavailable action checks and currency mismatches are excluded from high/low rankings. Large changes are flagged but retained because genuine market losses can be large. Other corporate actions can remain. Rankings are descriptive, not evidence of event causation.

The selection count is rounded up and all ties at the cutoff are retained. Missing or nonpositive market caps and ambiguous duplicate listings are excluded before selecting the top 10%. ETFs are excluded where explicitly identifiable. Multiple share classes remain separate listings. The source's company-level market cap can apply to more than one class; it is not necessarily free-float market cap.

Only information in the latest report strictly before each event selects the sample. Share identity is the exact BOS ticker and currency; missing, renamed or delisted securities are not replaced with later winners. Prior-year comparisons condition on event-time coverage and are not an investable strategy. The universe is selected BOS coverage, not the full exchange market.

Month labels identify the monthly archive slot; prices can be from the preceding business day or month. March 2019 uses a 12 March substitute. The archive begins July 2017, leaving earlier requested slots unavailable. Cross-country percentages are in local currencies, with no FX hedge or common-currency conversion.

Company names and lines use the supplied V1.2 colour master where identity matches. Unmapped companies use neutral Global Slate. Repeated colours use line patterns and exact ticker labels. In price-change mode, red/green heat-map colour encodes signed price change, capped at ±60% for colour intensity. In valuation modes, blue encodes the reported multiple as explained above. Printed values are uncapped.

Teach me: price return versus total return

A share rising from 100 to 110 has a 10% price return. A dividend can add to an investor's return even if the quoted price is unchanged. This study calculates changes from dated prices, so it excludes dividends. The separate site assumption about BOS's published YTD field does not apply to this price calculation. A stock split changes share units; retrieved split factors put prices on comparable units before calculating the change.

Sources and dates

Bank of Singapore dated equity coverage PDFs supply prices, market caps and coverage. Yahoo Finance historical corporate actions supplement split checks. Official event links appear within each event.

Event markers provide context, not proof of causation. Published prices and market caps are rounded; coverage and other company events can affect comparisons.
